body: Some stretches of life are simply grey. You do not have to explain yours to anyone.
Low days are part of being a person. Having one, or many in a row, does not mean you are failing.
You don't have to feel better today. You only have to get through today.
It is fine if nothing sounds fun right now. Flat is a feeling too, and it is allowed.
Getting out of bed was harder than it looks from outside. You did it, or you will, and both count.
There may be no clear reason for feeling this way. A mood does not need a reason to be real.
Heavy is the word some people use. If that fits you today, carry only what you must.
Not every day needs to be useful. A slow, quiet day still belongs to you.
Smiling for other people can be tiring when you are low. You may put the smile down when alone.
Everything taking more effort than usual is not laziness. It is what a low stretch does.
If the dishes are piling up, that says nothing about your character. It says you are tired.
Whatever you managed today was done with less fuel than usual. That makes it worth more.
Feeling far away from people, even ones you love, is common in a low spell. They are still there.
Today can be a small day. Small days are allowed to exist.
Your mind may be telling you unkind things at the moment. A low mood does not always tell the truth.
Wanting to cancel everything is understandable. You could cancel some and keep one easy thing.
Tears with no clear cause are still honest tears. Let them out if they come.
Nobody is keeping score of how productive you are this week. You can stop keeping score too.
The afternoon can drag when you feel like this. It is fine to just let it pass.
Being kind to yourself may feel fake right now. It can still help a little, even when it feels fake.
Low moods often lie about how long they will last. You do not have to believe every forecast.
Rest is not giving up. Lying down for a while is a fair response to a heavy day.
Many people around you have had stretches like this and never said so. You are less alone than it seems.
Even your favourite things may feel dull just now. They have not gone, they are waiting.
Comparing yourself to brighter days is unfair on you. This is a different season with different rules.
Saying you are not okay is allowed, to one person or only to yourself.
Mornings might be the lowest point. If so, ask very little of yourself before noon.
A day spent mostly on the sofa is not a wasted life. It is one day, and you needed it.
Things that felt easy last year may feel steep now. Steep does not mean impossible, and slow is fine.
One month into this grey patch, you are still turning up for your days. That is not nothing.
Drink a glass of water now, before you read anything else. Small things first.
Open a window or a door for a few minutes. New air in the room is a quiet kind of help.
Stand outside for ten minutes, even on the doorstep. Daylight counts whether or not you walk.
Text one person a single line today. Hello is a complete message.
Wash your face and brush your teeth. On low days these are real achievements.
Eat something, even if it is plain. A piece of toast or fruit gives the afternoon a better chance.
Put on clean clothes, even if you stay home. It is a small signal to yourself that today counts.
Try a five minute walk, to the corner and back. You may turn round whenever you want.
Make your bed, or just pull the cover straight. One tidy surface can soften a room.
Choose one tiny job and set a timer for ten minutes. When it rings, you are free to stop.
Play one song you used to like. You do not have to enjoy it, only let it play.
Sit by the brightest window you have with a warm drink. That is the whole task.
Take a shower if you can. Warm water on your shoulders is a kind of comfort.
Write down one thing you did today, however small. Got up. Ate. Answered a message.
Step away from your phone for half an hour. Other people's best moments online are heavy on low days.
Water a plant, feed a pet or wipe one table. Looking after something small can steady you.
Go to bed and get up at about the same times this week. A plain rhythm holds you when mood does not.
Say good morning to one person, a neighbour or a shop worker. Brief contact still counts.
Stretch your arms above your head and breathe out slowly. Your body has been curled up too long.
Cook the simplest warm meal you know. Eggs, rice or soup are enough.
Leave the house once today, even to take out the rubbish. The door is the hardest part.
Tell a friend you are having a low spell, in plain words. You do not need to make it sound better.
Let light in as soon as you wake. Curtains open is a good first move.
Look for one small pleasant thing today: a taste, a colour, a sound. One is plenty.
Steady days are made of very ordinary pieces. Water, food, air, sleep. Keep to those.
Carry a small snack with you today. Low mood and an empty stomach are a hard pair.
Read one page of anything. A page is a fine amount.
Clear one small space, like the bedside table. A calm corner is easier to rest your eyes on.
Plan one easy thing for tomorrow, so the day has something in it. A walk or a call will do.
Ask someone to join you for a short walk. Side by side is easier than face to face.
Do one thing a little slower than usual today, like making tea. Slow is allowed.
Notice your breathing for three breaths. Nothing to change, only to notice.
If today went badly, the small steps are still there tomorrow. They do not run out.
Spend ten minutes somewhere with trees or water if one is near. Just being there is enough.
Two months of small steps on low days takes real effort. You have been making that effort.
Look back over the last nine weeks. On many of those days you did one small kind thing for yourself.
Early on, a glass of water felt like a big ask. You have asked more of yourself since, gently.
Maybe the grey has thinned in places. If it has not yet, your steadiness inside it still matters.
Your low days have not beaten you. You have met each one and reached the evening.
Remember the week when everything felt uphill. You kept walking, slowly, and here you are.
Some colour may be coming back to small things. Notice it without holding on too tightly.
By now you know a few things that help a little. That knowledge was hard won, and it is yours.
A lighter day does not mean the hard days were not real. Both belong to the same honest story.
People you reached out to are still there. Those threads are stronger for having been used.
Low moods may return from time to time. You can meet them knowing more than you did before.
Thinking about next month may be easier now than it was. Even a vague thought of it is a step.
The habits you kept on the worst days were the strongest ones. They were built under real weight.
Whatever pace you moved at was the right one. Slow progress is still a road travelled.
Consider one thing you might like to try again soon. A hobby, a place, a person. No rush at all.
You have been patient with yourself more often than before. That patience is a skill now.
Not every morning is light yet, and you no longer expect it to be. That is a calmer way to live.
Hope does not have to be loud. A small wish for a good cup of tea tomorrow is hope enough.
Many of the hardest days are behind you in the calendar. You crossed them one by one.
Looking forward, keep the door open for good moments. They tend to arrive without knocking.
If you need more support than small steps can give, asking for it is a strong and sensible act.
Future grey days will find you with a short list of things that help. Keep that list close.
Keep the simple things going: water, daylight, one message, enough sleep. They carried you this far.
Almost three months on, you know yourself in low weather. Few lessons are learned so honestly.
Kindness toward yourself started as an effort. Perhaps now and then it comes a little easier.
These daily messages are close to their end. What you practised in them stays with you.
Tomorrow is the last note. Thank you for opening these on days when opening anything was hard.
Three months of days, grey ones and lighter ones, are behind you. Go on gently, at your own pace.
